deviations.why: A3 (toolchain drift). xmlsec HEAD (1.3.13 dev) now enables hardening flags by default, incl. -fcf-protection=full. The pinned base image's AFL++ afl-cc treats any -fcf-protection* argument as a CFI-sanitizer request (src/afl-cc.c: '-fcf-protection' -> have_cfisan), so it injects -flto -fvisibility=hidden and emits LLVM bitcode objects; the non-LTO libtool link of libxmlsec1.la then fails with '.libs/app.o: file not recognized'. Verified in the image: adding only -fcf-protection=full to an afl-clang-fast compile of src/app.c turns ELF output into LLVM IR bitcode.
deviations.rationale: Uses xmlsec's own supported configure switch; no source or harness change and no change to OSS-Fuzz-composed CFLAGS/sanitizer/-O. It drops xmlsec's project-added hardening set (-fstack-protector-strong, -fPIE, -fcf-protection=full, -fstack-clash-protection, -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, -pie/-z relro/-z now), which restores the flag set OSS-Fuzz built xmlsec with before the hardening default landed. There is no narrower knob for -fcf-protection alone short of patching configure.ac (F3) or afl-cc (F5). Reviewer: confirm dropping the whole hardening set is acceptable (ASan supersedes stack-protector/FORTIFY detection). Controller ruling R7: marked affects_measurement=true because xmlsec's own default hardening flags (-fcf-protection, -fstack-protector-strong, _FORTIFY_SOURCE, ...) are off in this build, so the compiled code differs from what xmlsec's configure would produce; OSS-Fuzz's own xmlsec build has been broken since 2026-09-30 with the same toolchain, so no OSS-Fuzz-exact build exists to match. A crash found on this build should be re-checked on a hardening-enabled build at write-up time.
